subject: history
title: Thatcherism to Blair 1979-1997
welcome_lead: From monetarism and miners to New Labour's landslide.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on Thatcher 1979-90, Major 1990-97 and the Blair victory of May 1997.
final_note: You can evaluate Thatcherism's legacy and the emergence of New Labour.

concepts.def: Mix of monetarism, privatisation, deregulation, anti-union legislation and Atlanticism associated with Margaret Thatcher, PM 1979-90.
Brief war (April-June 1982) against Argentina over the Falkland Islands, boosting Thatcher's popularity.
Year-long NUM strike led by Arthur Scargill against pit closures; ended without agreement in March 1985.
Sale of state-owned firms (BT 1984, British Gas 1986, water 1989, electricity 1990, rail 1994-97); raised approximately £50 billion.
Community Charge introduced 1989 (Scotland) and 1990 (England/Wales); riots in March 1990 contributed to Thatcher's fall in November.

walkthroughs.body_html: Geoffrey Howe's 1981 budget tightened amid recession (unemployment >3 million). The Falklands (April-June 1982) revived Thatcher; the 1983 election delivered a 144-seat majority. Privatisation began with BT (1984). The defeat of the Miners' Strike (March 1985) broke union power, helped by the 1980, 1982 and 1984 Employment Acts. The Single European Act (1986) and Big Bang (October 1986) deregulated finance. The Poll Tax destroyed her premiership; she resigned on 22 November 1990.

Major won the April 1992 election but Black Wednesday (16 September 1992) crashed sterling out of the ERM. Maastricht (ratified 1993), 'Back to Basics' sleaze and Conservative divisions over Europe sapped support. Rail privatisation (1994-97) and BSE (1996) added difficulties.

John Smith's death (1994) brought Blair to the leadership; Clause IV was rewritten in 1995. The 1997 manifesto pledged adherence to Conservative spending limits and a windfall tax on utilities. On 1 May 1997, Labour won 418 seats, a landslide that opened a thirteen-year era of New Labour government.

mcqs.q: Why did Caribbean migrants come to Britain in 1948 on the Windrush?
options: Windrush migrants were illegal immigrants from outside the empire.
Britain faced post-war labour shortages; the 1948 British Nationality Act gave Commonwealth citizens UK residency rights and Caribbean migrants answered the call to rebuild.
Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
Hitler called off the attack to invade the USSR immediately.

mcqs.q: Why did Britain restrict Commonwealth immigration from 1962?
options: Rising public hostility, political pressure, and economic concerns led to the 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act introducing voucher controls, followed by tighter restrictions in 1968 and 1971.
Britain restricted Commonwealth immigration because there was no work available.
Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
